# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 4
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 4

---

*[King Gundaphorus returns and finds no palace. Thomas is imprisoned. The king's brother Gad dies and sees the palace in heaven. He returns to life.]*

1. But after some time the king returned from the other country and inquired of his friends about the palace.

2. And they said to him: "He built no palace, O king; but he went around and gave to the poor, and he says that he has built you a palace in heaven."

3. Then the king was very angry, and he commanded Thomas and Abbanes to be seized, and he said that they should be cast into prison.

4. And they were cast into prison, and the king thought about what kind of death he would put Thomas to.

5. Now the king had a brother, Gad by name, who fell ill and died at that time.

6. And the king was very sorrowful about his brother, for he loved him greatly.

7. And when Gad died and his body was being laid out, angels took his soul and carried it up into heaven, and they showed him many dwelling-places there.

8. And he came to that most beautiful palace which Thomas had built with his charitable deeds, and he desired to dwell in it.

9. And the angels said to him: "This palace is the one which the Christian whom your brother imprisoned has built for your brother."

10. And Gad said: "I beg you, permit me to go back and buy this palace from my brother, for my brother does not know what it is and he will sell it to me."

11. And they permitted him to return and he returned to life.

12. And when he returned, his brother was sitting beside the body.

13. And Gad said: "Brother, the slave whom you imprisoned — I beg you, give him to me. For I want to buy something from him that he has."

14. And the king said: "What is there left for him to give you?"

15. And Gad said: "Show me this slave and I will tell you what I have seen."

16. And the king was astonished and ordered Thomas to be brought out of prison.

17. And when he came, Gad fell at his feet and said: "I beg you, give me the upper chamber of the palace which you have built in heaven."

18. And Thomas said: "I cannot give it, for it belongs to your brother, to whom I built it."

19. And Gad said: "I beg you, sell it to me."

20. And Thomas said: "I cannot sell it. But your brother, if he so wishes, can give it to you."

21. And the king understood what had happened and received the faith and was baptized.

---
*EMET note: The story of Gad is the narrative resolution of the palace deception. The Syriac *'aliyya* (upper chamber) is architecturally specific — the best room, the place of honor in a Semitic house.*
